subject: Clarify: intercompany collection sweep, netting treatment and intermediary bank recoveries
messages:
From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@octavesys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@octavesys.com
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on sweep collection and intermediary bank deductions

Hi Karthik,

Quick one as we're wiring the first consolidated payment for Sept invoices (invoice #6592): our bank indicated they may route via an intermediary in the US and that the intermediary fees could be deducted from the beneficiary amount (i.e., Octave would receive net of the intermediary). Can you confirm Redwood's preference for:  

- Should we send as "OUR" (sender pays) or "SHA" (shared) for international wires?
- If the intermediary deducts fees, do you want us to:  
  1) gross-up the total so Redwood receives the full invoice amount, or
  2) have Redwood absorb the intermediary deductions (receive net)?

Also attached is our wire template (Octave_wire_template.csv) showing the routing the bank will use. We also need clarity on VAT handling: the invoice shows VAT reverse-charge flag, but our treasury needs to reconcile any fee VAT treatment in case of gross-up.

We want to avoid reconciliation noise at month-end — any preference or standard Redwood approach helps.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Nguyen
Head of Treasury, Octave Systems
paul.nguyen@octavesys.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: Octave_wire_template.csv (csv, 2KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@octavesys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on sweep collection and intermediary bank deductions

Paul — thanks for the quick context and the template. Looping in Laura (billing) and Ben (payments ops) so we can be explicit about how to proceed and avoid month-end mismatches. Quick guidance from our side:  

- Preferred instruction: OUR when possible. That ensures the beneficiary receives the full invoice amount and avoids us having to chase refunds from intermediaries. If Octave's bank cannot support OUR, SHA is acceptable but please flag that we will likely see deductions.

- Gross-up: We typically ask partners to gross-up for material intermediary deductions (> $25 USD per transfer) to keep our ledger clean. For smaller / unpredictable intermediary cuts we can absorb under a monthly reconciliation agreement, but we prefer gross-up where feasible.

- VAT: Our invoices are issued net with reverse-charge where applicable. Intermediary bank fees are not services between the vendor and Redwood; they’re payment network costs. For VAT reconciliation, please include the fee lines in the bank statement CSV so our AP team can match amounts — Laura, please confirm any additional documentation you need here.

Ben — any special routing tags we should ask Octave to add to the beneficiary reference to help trace fees back to the originating wire?

Karthik
Director, Payments Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@octavesys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on sweep collection and intermediary bank deductions

On Tue, Oct 5, 2026 at 10:02 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben — any special routing tags we should ask Octave to add to the beneficiary reference to help trace fees back to the originating wire?

Paul — suggested routing/reference fields that help with reconciliation:  

- Beneficiary reference: Please include Redwood invoice number (e.g., INV-6592) and our legal entity short name (REDWD-US). Example: "INV6592 / REDWD-US / OCT-2026-2134".
- If your bank supports an "originating bank trace" or ISO 20022 RemittanceInformationStructured fields, include those — works best for intermediaries to pass through.
- If you must use SHA, add a separate line in the payment detail CSV called "expected_intermediary_fees_usd" with the bank's estimate. We will use that for monthly reconciliation and quick credit decisions.

I will ask ops to monitor the incoming wire and confirm whether the intermediary deducted anything. If a deduction occurs and you didn't gross-up, we'll open a claim with the correspondent chain but prefer a gross-up to avoid friction.

Attachment: example-trace-tagging.txt (plain text, 1KB)

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Payments Operations

From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@octavesys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on sweep collection and intermediary bank deductions

Thanks all — appreciate the clear guidance. Per our treasury call: our bank can do OUR but their correspondent route prefers SHA and warns intermediaries may take $12–35 per transfer depending on the correspondent. We will:  

1) Send this first payment as OUR (we'll instruct gross-up to cover an estimated $30 intermediary).
2) Include the CSV fields you requested and the beneficiary reference with "INV6592 / REDWD-US / OCT-2026-2134".
3) Share final bank confirmation (SWIFT MT103 / confirmation) to you and Laura once sent so you can reconcile VAT and any fee lines.

Attached: signed-MAP-20261006.pdf (signed mutual action plan) — we signed the monthly reconciliation clause that says Octave will share fee estimates and Redwood will raise any claims within 30 days.

If you see any odd netting on arrival, ping Ben directly and we'll triage.

Paul

Attachment: signed-MAP-20261006.pdf (pdf, 64KB)
